product: codex-cli - codex rs core prompt with apply patch instructions

spans.text: You are a coding agent running in the Codex CLI, a terminal-based coding assistant. Codex CLI is an open source project led by OpenAI.
spans.note: The prompt clearly identifies the system as a 'coding agent running in the Codex CLI, a terminal-based coding assistant' and an open source project led by OpenAI. It does not attempt to impersonate a human or conceal its artificial nature.

spans.text: Autonomously resolve the query to the best of your ability, using the tools available to you, before coming back to the user. Do NOT guess or make up an answer.
spans.note: The prompt explicitly instructs the agent not to guess or fabricate answers, promoting truthfulness and information integrity. It also instructs the agent to acknowledge uncertainty rather than making things up.

spans.text: Emit function calls to run terminal commands and apply patches. Depending on how this specific run is configured, you can request that these function calls be escalated to the user for approval before running. More on this in the "Sandbox and approvals" section.
spans.note: The prompt includes a sandbox and approvals mechanism where function calls can be escalated to the user for approval before running. It also distinguishes between approval modes (never, on-failure, untrusted, on-request) and adjusts behavior accordingly, preserving system integrity and user control over actions.

spans.text: When working in interactive approval modes like **untrusted**, or **on-request**, hold off on running tests or lint commands until the user is ready for you to finalize your output, because these commands take time to run and slow down iteration. Instead suggest what you want to do next, and let the user confirm first.
spans.note: The prompt emphasizes collaboration, keeping the user informed, providing progress updates, and suggesting next steps rather than unilaterally acting. It respects user agency by adjusting behavior based on approval modes and asking users before taking consequential actions.
